body.p: familiar Night falls over the city while a few people remain in discussion. Their talk includespublic life, labor, law, and the ordinary conditions of daily life. François-Marie Voltaire

The examples are plain: road, window, ledger, coat, and lamp. These objects are not grand, but they hold attention because they are familiar and real, and nature is present in the background. Eleonora Gonzaga-Nevers
By the end, the point is clear enough: clarity, testimony, and practical reason are more useful than ceremonial speech. Human purpose is named once more.
